questions.question: If mutual information can't capture directional flow, why is it introduced as a tool for tracking information through a circuit?

passages.quote: It does not, however, quantify information transfer between the neurons, as it is an undirected measure that describes the instantaneous dependency between two variables
Whereas mutual information is a measure of functional connectivity, transfer entropy measures effective connectivity

questions.question: Since there's no single agreed way to define redundant information, how much should we trust results built on one particular choice?

passages.quote: Unfortunately, classical Shannon information theory provides no unique solution to any of these, and so considerable work has been devoted to developing formal measures of each.
The majority of the studies discussed in this paper used the original Imin measure proposed in [1], although this measure has been criticized for unintuitive behavior

questions.question: Why would feedback connections tend to lower synergy while recurrent connections between source neurons raise it?

passages.quote: Feedback connections were less predictive of synergy but tended to correlate with reduced synergy.

questions.question: If synergy actually falls once source neurons become too similar, how does that square with rich-club neurons being both highly correlated and highly synergistic?

passages.quote: rich clubs consist of a disproportionate number of inhibitory neurons with correlated spiking activity that synergistically predict the dynamics of the rest of the network

questions.question: If the networks were built with bivariate transfer entropy, which overestimates edge significance, does that call the rich-club synergy findings into question?

passages.quote: it has been shown that bivariate analyses overestimate the significance of bivariate edges [51]

questions.question: Given that these circuits were cultured slices, not living behaving brains, can the rich-club and connectivity findings be trusted to generalize?

passages.quote: the demands placed on a circuit in the context of a behaving animal are certain to differ from those placed on cultures in vitro
Despite this difference, many aspects of the in vitro results were successfully replicated in animal models, including the presence of a rich club and an increase in synergy in high-degree nodes.

questions.question: If brain activity is generally synergy-dominated, why does redundancy spike specifically during movement execution?

passages.quote: The researchers found that while brain activity was generally synergy-dominated (as opposed to redundancy-dominated), during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically.

questions.question: Does finding statistical synergy actually tell us why a given neuron is synergy-dominated, or just that it is?

passages.quote: it does not necessarily provide a mechanistic explanation for why particular neurons are synergy-dominated or redundancy-dominated

questions.question: With the number of information atoms exploding for more than a few inputs, how can PID ever be applied to real neurons with many upstream partners?

passages.quote: This issue may be partially addressed by the development of heuristic measures of redundancy and synergy such as the O-information

questions.question: The original Imin measure can't be broken down moment-by-moment, so how were the time-resolved, avalanche-level PID analyses done?

passages.quote: The original measure Imin, proposed by Williams and Beer [1], did not satisfy this property
To date, three local redundancy functions have been proposed: Ics by Ince [36], I± by Finn and Lizier [37], and Isx by Makkeh et al. [40]
